lang_en:
Four of us got one November weekend off, and Rohan picked Shimla.
He wanted Mall Road at night and a hotel on it.
Meher wanted quiet, so nothing got booked while they argued.
That went on for days, until Meher read one line aloud.
Nobody spoke, and a pressure cooker whistled in the kitchen.
NakshIQ called Mall Road weekends a nightmare, and named where Shimla's locals escape.
The catch is zero Mall Road and only a few stays, so not for shoppers.
Then Rohan saw Chail's cricket ground, the world's highest, and forgot Mall Road.
Travel intelligence is knowing who a place isn't for.
NakshIQ.
lang_hi:
हम चारों को नवंबर का एक ही वीकेंड मिला, और रोहन ने शिमला चुन लिया।
उसे रात वाला मॉल रोड चाहिए था, और होटल भी ठीक उसी पर।
मेहर को सुकून चाहिए था, तो दोनों की बहस में कुछ बुक ही नहीं हुआ।
ये कई दिन चला, फिर एक दिन मेहर ने एक लाइन पढ़कर सुनाई।
कोई कुछ नहीं बोला, बस किचन में कुकर की सीटी बजी।
NakshIQ पर लिखा था कि वीकेंड पर मॉल रोड का बुरा हाल होता है, और ये भी कि शिमला वाले खुद कहाँ घूमने जाते हैं।
बस दिक्कत ये कि वहाँ मॉल रोड है ही नहीं, रुकने की जगहें भी गिनी चुनी, तो शॉपिंग करने वालों के लिए ये जगह नहीं।
फिर रोहन ने चैल का क्रिकेट ग्राउंड देखा, दुनिया का सबसे ऊँचा, और मॉल रोड भूल गया।
ट्रैवल इंटेलिजेंस है ये जानना कि कोई जगह किसके लिए नहीं है।
NakshIQ.

shots: Late afternoon in a small flat: four friends in their late 20s, two men and two women, sit around a low table with a laptop and phones, seen from behind and the side, faces turned away, every screen turned away from camera.

Medium shot in the same flat, late afternoon: one woman sits looking down at the phone in her hands, seen over her shoulder from behind, the screen blurred, the other three sitting still and facing her.
Late afternoon in the same flat's small kitchen: a steel pressure cooker on a gas stove, a thin jet of steam rising from its whistle, no people in frame.
Late afternoon, wide from behind: the four friends walk slowly along the edge of a flat green cricket ground on a hilltop, tall pine forest all around it, nobody else on the ground.

Late afternoon: one of the men stands alone on the grass just inside the boundary of the cricket ground, seen from behind, hands in his jacket pockets, looking out at the forest, the other three small and still at the boundary behind him.
Very wide in late afternoon light: the whole cricket ground on its hilltop ringed by dark pine forest, the four friends small on the grass, no buildings, shops or other people in frame.
